raw_response:
I am 70 years old this year, and my back isn't what it used to be. I have been farming our 10.1 mu for 15 years now, since I was 55, when my husband couldn't manage the heavy work anymore. Our two sons work construction in Shijiazhuang, sending some money home, but I have my daughter-in-law and grandson here with me. Seven mouths to feed, and every yuan matters. I split the land into 6 mu for wheat followed by maize, and 4.1 mu for cotton. The wheat-maize gives us grain and stability, and cotton brings cash income, though at my age I couldn't handle more than 4 mu of cotton even with my daughter-in-law's help.

For the **winter wheat**, I planted it last October 12th with about 15 kg per mu of improved seed. I already put down compound fertilizer then and gave it the overwinter irrigation in November. Now it is April and the wheat is at jointing stage. The extension station recommends topdressing around this time, so I'll spread about 10 kg per mu of urea. I already applied base fertilizer with roughly 8 kg of nitrogen equivalent last fall, so the total nitrogen for the year will be about 18 kg per mu. If it doesn't rain by early May, I'll irrigate once more before harvest—that makes three irrigations total for the wheat. I expect about 430 kg per mu at harvest in early June if the weather holds. Last year I got 420 kg, and this year looks similar.

For **summer maize**, the window is always tight—maybe five to seven days after wheat harvest in early June. I'll hire the combine for the wheat, then we'll get the maize in fast. I buy hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu, which costs around 45 yuan per mu. At planting I put compound fertilizer in the furrow, about 35 kg per mu, and then side-dress urea at jointing in late July. Total nitrogen around 16 kg per mu. I'll irrigate twice if it's dry—once right after planting to help germination, and once at flowering in August. I usually get about 480 kg per mu, which is enough for our household needs plus some to sell.

For **cotton**, I am planting around April 20th. I use about 1.5 kg per mu of the same improved variety my neighbor used last year—she had good results. I'll plow and harrow the field first, then put down compound fertilizer as base, about 30 kg per mu. Total nitrogen for cotton will be about 14 kg per mu, with a urea topdress at flowering in early July. I irrigate twice—once after planting to help it settle, and once in July when it is flowering. Cotton needs more pesticide than grain: herbicide at planting, insecticide two or three times for aphids and bollworms, and maybe fungicide if it gets humid. My daughter-in-law and I will pick by hand through September and October, three or four rounds. We might hire help for two days at peak picking if my arthritis flares up. I expect about 230 kg per mu of seed cotton.

Now, about money. I have about 2,500 yuan in cash from selling last year's grain, but my total input costs will be over 3,000 yuan. I will need to borrow 500 yuan from my sister, or cut back somewhere. The extension people say I could use more fertilizer on the cotton, but last year I tried a bit more and didn't see much difference. I'd rather have some cash in hand for my grandson's school fees than gamble on a slightly higher yield. That's how it is when you're old and the farm is small—you find what works, you don't chase perfection.
